name: Bialgebra
summary: A phase-free X-spider followed by a phase-free Z-spider can be commuted past one another.
description:
The bialgebra rule expresses that the Z- and X-spiders form a (scaled) bialgebra, which is also called *strong complementarity*. A two-input X-spider (XOR) followed by a two-output Z-spider (COPY) is equal to first copying both inputs and then taking XORs pairwise. This is one of the main reasons that the phase-free fragment is so expressive: it captures the interaction of XOR and COPY, i.e. linear maps over the field with two elements.

See the [generalised bialgebra](../bialgebra-generalised/) rule for spiders with any number of legs.
